title: Miracles
lead: The Bible tells of mighty acts of God that break the usual course of things: the signs and wonders of the Exodus, the deeds of Elijah and Elisha, and above all the healings, exorcisms, raisings of the dead and acts over nature done by Jesus and later by his apostles. Scripture calls them wonders, signs and mighty works, and presents them as signs of God's power and, in the Gospels, of his kingdom drawing near.

sections.b: The Old Testament gathers miracles around times of crisis. Moses' signs and the plagues show God's power over Egypt (Exodus 4–12), and the sea is parted (Exodus 14). Elijah and Elisha multiply food, heal a foreign commander's skin disease and raise a widow's son (1 Kings 17; 2 Kings 4–5). The Gospels often echo these stories.
sections.refs: Exodus 7:3; Exodus 14:21–31; 1 Kings 17:8–24; 2 Kings 4:18–44; 2 Kings 5:1–14; Deuteronomy 13:1–3

sections.b: The Gospels report healings (skin disease, paralysis, blindness, bleeding), exorcisms, raisings of the dead, and acts over nature (stilling the storm, walking on water, the feedings). Matthew gathers ten of them in chapters 8–9, after the Sermon on the Mount, and Jesus answers John the Baptist by listing them in the words of Isaiah (Matthew 11:4–5; Isaiah 35:5–6).
sections.refs: Matthew 8:1–9:34; Matthew 11:4–5; Isaiah 35:5–6; Mark 6:45–52; John 2:11; John 20:30–31

sections.b: Traditional readers take the miracles as real events that show who Jesus is. Historians of many views agree that Jesus was known in his lifetime as a healer and exorcist, even by opponents who said he worked by Beelzebul (Matthew 12:24). Since the Enlightenment some have explained them naturally or as legends; others read them mainly as symbols. Churches also differ over whether such gifts continue today.

Acts reports that the apostles healed and raised the dead in Jesus' name, as he had sent the Twelve to do (Matthew 10:8). Paul lists healing and miracles among the gifts of the Spirit and speaks of "signs and wonders" done through him.
sections.refs: Acts 3:1–10; Acts 9:36–42; Acts 19:11–12; Romans 15:19; 1 Corinthians 12:9–10; 2 Corinthians 12:12
